liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Reviewer found the opening Bucket tight and rocking [16]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Sugaree was sweetly played and mellowed the crowd, with Jerry standing out on guitar [16]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Scarlet/Fire pairing as really good [13]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 other source): The Neville Brothers play from the drums through Johnny B. Goode [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mardi Gras Festival Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Willy And The Hand Jive**: back after 947 archived shows (5029 days); rare: 7 archived performances [24]
- **Fire On The Bayou**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Africa**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Run JOe**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **People Say ?**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Caravan**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Sitting In Limbo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Hey Pocky Way [24]

## The recordings

- **gd86-02-12.beyer.connor.3302.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 28 songs; 175 min; rated 4.38/5 by 8 [1]
- **gd1986-02-12.sbd.bertha.21614.shnf**: soundboard; 16 songs; 116 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard immaculate, with powerful bass and all instruments very forward, like a studio recording; Notes warn of a sound problem during Don't Ease Me In [2][21]
- **gd1986-02-12.170343.sbd.marcus.menke.miller.clugston.flac1648**: soundboard; 16 songs; 121 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1986-02-12.sbd.miller.81517.flac16**: soundboard; 16 songs; 121 min; rated 3.29/5 by 7 [4]

## Around the show

- The Neville Brothers played alongside the band, which the reviewer says shows in the setlist [12]
- Reviewer went to the first four of five nights and says earlier nights left few brain cells intact [15]
- The show fell on Ash Wednesday, the night after a Mardi Gras blowout on Fat Tuesday [16]
- Steve Marcus told the reviewer late in the second set to stay after the show [17]
- After the venue was cleared, the Dead, the Nevilles and others jammed on stage until 7:30 next morning [17]
- Because of a curfew, the show runs under two hours [21]
- The Neville Brothers' set is included as disc 1 of this release [1]
- Members of the Neville Brothers played on the marked portions of the show [2]
- Reviewer rates the Chinese New Year shows as hotter than the Mardi Gras shows, which were still solid [15]
- Reviewer calls the February 11 second set odd, an exception among the solid Mardi Gras shows [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd86-02-12.beyer.connor.3302.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD> Beyer Dynamic M88's> Sony TCD5M (CM)> Nak DR-10 (Playback)> Midiman Flying Cow 24bit/48kHz A/D> RME Digi96/8> Steinberg's Wavelab 3.0 (bit resolution &… [1]. Also: Reviewer says this show was a long-time rarity among tape traders and newly appeared on the archive [13]
- **gd1986-02-12.sbd.bertha.21614.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: SBD>>(?)>>Wav(EAC)>>DAW(Bertha)>>CDA/SHN [2]. Also: Reviewer praises this soundboard as an extraordinary remaster [21]
- **gd1986-02-12.170343.sbd.marcus.menke.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Steve Marcus; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Steve Marcus' Master Soundboard Cassettes > Sony WM-D6C (Maxell MX-90) [3]
- **gd1986-02-12.sbd.miller.81517.flac16**: taped by This is a Joani Walker master and Paul Scotton provided Charlie with the tapes.; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90/Dolby B) D [4]. Also: Charlie Connor's recording: Beyer M88 mics to cassette master, then Wavelab to CD [4]
